title: Normal form of the specified positive-iterate scheme/Galois comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its fixed algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\Phi$, $g_\sigma$, and $g=g_\gamma=g_\sigma^{-1}$ be its scheme, arithmetic Galois, and geometric Galois Frobenii [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Write $F_X$ for absolute $p$-power Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by an integer prime to $p$, and work in $D_R=D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For $m\geq1$, put $H=F_X^{am}$. Then $X$ has characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p] and
$$\Phi^m=g^m\circ H=H\circ g^m.$$
Let $d_R:L(\Phi^m)_R^*\xrightarrow{\sim}LH_R^*L(g^m)_R^*$ be the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $\Phi^m=g^m\circ H$, using canonical constant-section coefficient identifications. Let $\tau_R^{(am)}:LH_R^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D_R}$ be the specified iterated absolute-Frobenius trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. For the specified multiplicative comparison $\kappa_R^{(m)}$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], normalized by that same trivialization, one has
$$\kappa^{(m)}_{R,K}=\tau^{(am)}_{R,L(g^m)_R^*K}\circ d_{R,K}$$
for every $K\in D_R$. The equality concerns the specified multiplicative iterate and the single exponent $am$ trivialization, including $m=1$; all scheme-map equalities are equalities of underlying scheme morphisms and impose no $k$-linearity on $g$.

proof.text: The field $k_0$ has characteristic $p$ by [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements]. The composite structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ from [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] gives a unital map $k_0\to\mathcal O_X(U)$ for each open $U$. It takes $p\cdot1=0$ to $p\cdot1=0$. Thus $X$ has characteristic $p$ in [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p], including when $X$ is empty.

source.place: First paragraph: applicability of absolute Frobenius to the geometric fibre

proof.text: For every $r\geq1$, put $H_r=F_X^{ar}$. By [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] this is absolute $q^r$-power Frobenius. The statement of [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] gives $H_r=g_\sigma^r\circ\Phi^r=\Phi^r\circ g_\sigma^r$. The maps $g$ and $g_\sigma$ of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] are inverse: on each base-changed affine chart their ring maps are $u\otimes b\mapsto u\otimes\sigma^{-1}(b)$ and $u\otimes b\mapsto u\otimes\sigma(b)$, whose composites fix every tensor. Therefore $\Phi^r=g^r\circ H_r=H_r\circ g^r$, by composing the two factorization equalities with $g^r$. In particular $H_n$ commutes with $g^m$ for all $m,n\geq1$: $H_n=H_1^n$, and $H_1$ commutes with $g$. These are underlying scheme-map equalities.

source.place: First paragraph: factorization; second paragraph: the same factorization for positive powers

proof.text: Use the canonical constant-section coefficient maps, which are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Their identification for a composite is the composite identification, by [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] applies to all the endomorphisms above with this one coefficient convention. Its comparisons satisfy the associativity equation in [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence]. Consequently expanding a composite of three or more maps by successive binary comparisons is independent of parenthesization: apply that equation to change one adjacent parenthesization at a time. Below all identifications of words of pullback functors mean these comparisons, and interchanging two commuting maps means comparing both words with the pullback of their common composite.

proof.text: Write $T_r=L(\Phi^r)_R^*$, $P_r=L(H_r)_R^*$ and $G_r=L(g^r)_R^*$. Step 2 and Step 3 give $d_r:T_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_rG_r$; this is exactly $d_R$ when $r=m$. Let $t_r=\tau_R^{(ar)}:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$, using [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site] and the explicit relative-Frobenius normalization in [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback]. Define the candidate $\beta_{r,K}=t_{r,G_rK}\circ d_{r,K}$. Each is a natural isomorphism. For $r=1$, the specified normalization in the question is precisely the source's displayed construction: first use $\Phi=gH_1$, then cancel $H_1$ by this trivialization. Thus $\beta_1=\kappa_R$. It remains to show that this candidate family is multiplicative; only the multiplicative-iterate assertion, not any unstated normal-form clause, will be taken from [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison].

proof.text:
Apply the addition clause of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] with $b_1=am$ and $b_2=an$. Under Step 3's comparisons it gives $t_{m+n,K}=t_{n,K}\circ t_{m,P_nK}$. Apply its pullback-naturality clause with $X=Y$, $u=g^m$ and $b=an$. These hypotheses hold: $X$ is of characteristic $p$ by Step 1, $g^m$ is a scheme morphism by [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and $R$ is finite commutative. No $k$-linearity is required. For the canonical interchange $e_{m,n}:G_mP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_nG_m$, the equation is
$$t_{n,G_mK}\circ e_{m,n,K}=G_m(t_{n,K}).$$
The trivializations here are the specified ones, since the cited statement identifies its $b=1$ trivialization with [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site] and its $b$-th one with the $b$-fold iterate.

proof.text:
Fix $m,n\geq1$ and $K$. By Step 2,
$$\Phi^{m+n}=(g^nH_n)(g^mH_m)=g^{m+n}H_{m+n}.$$
Thus [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence] identifies $d_{m+n}$ with the expansion
$$T_{m+n}\simeq T_mT_n\xrightarrow{d_m d_n}P_mG_mP_nG_n\xrightarrow{P_m(e_{m,n})G_n}P_mP_nG_mG_n.$$
Here the middle interchange is exactly Step 5's comparison, because its two words represent $H_n g^m=g^mH_n$. Naturality of $t_m$ at $G_m(d_{n,K})$ moves the expansion of $T_nK$ past $t_m$. In these coordinates the composite $G_m(\beta_{n,K})\circ\beta_{m,T_nK}$ is
$$G_m(t_{n,G_nK})\circ t_{m,G_mP_nG_nK}.$$
Step 5 replaces its first factor by $t_{n,G_mG_nK}\circ e_{m,n,G_nK}$. Naturality of $t_m$ at $e_{m,n,G_nK}$ gives
$$e_{m,n,G_nK}\circ t_{m,G_mP_nG_nK}=t_{m,P_nG_mG_nK}\circ P_m(e_{m,n,G_nK}).$$
The resulting expression is therefore $t_{n,G_mG_nK}\circ t_{m,P_nG_mG_nK}$ after that interchange. Step 5's addition law makes this $t_{m+n,G_{m+n}K}$. Restoring the comparison of domains proves
$$\beta_{m+n,K}=G_m(\beta_{n,K})\circ\beta_{m,T_nK}.$$
Now induct on $r\geq1$. Step 4 gives the base $\beta_1=\kappa_R$. If $\beta_r=\kappa_R^{(r)}$, the formula just proved with $(m,n)=(r,1)$ and the multiplicative-iterate clause of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] give $\beta_{r+1}=\kappa_R^{(r+1)}$. Hence for $r=m$ the claimed equality is $\kappa_{R,K}^{(m)}=t_{m,G_mK}\circ d_{m,K}$, with the single exponent $am$ trivialization, as required.
